test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 09 Dec 2022 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
**Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.**

Neither the teachers (or the principal likes the new budget) cuts.

options.text: either the principal likes the new budget
or the principal like the new budget
nor the principal like the new budget
nor the principal likes the new budget

solution:
The correct answer is option 4), i.e., 'nor the principal likes the new budget.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in Part (or the principal likes the new budget) of the sentence.
 
• As per instructions, the remaining portion of the sentence is correct.
 
• According to the rules of correlative conjunctions, ‘either ...... or’, ‘neither ..... nor’, ‘both ..... and’, ‘not only ...... but also’, ‘though .... yet’, ‘whether...or’ are used in pairs.
 
• The given sentence begins with **'Neither' **so** 'nor' **will be used with it.
 
• **Option 3,** "nor the principal like the new budget," has **incorrect subject-verb agreement.**
 
• If two subjects are joined by **"neither...nor", **the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. In this case, the subject nearest to the verb is '**principal**' which is singular. Thus, a singular helping verb is needed i.e. '**likes**'.
 
• **Option 4,** "nor the principal likes the new budget," is absolutely correct.
 
• Therefore, in the erroneous part, the use of 'or' in the sentence should be replaced with 'nor' to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Correct sentence:__ *Neither the teachers __**nor the principal likes the new budget**__ cuts.*
